ambiguities_or_notes: French original and Russian editorial rendering are both translated in source order, with all three source page markers, envelope address, editorial publication note, and three surviving Markdown footnotes represented.
The source language metadata says ru although the first half is French; English metadata records both fr and ru and the Russian source is left unchanged.

The French half retains a bare note numeral 2 after the prince’s daughter; official volume 59 confirms it is a printed note marker, but its original-French definition is displaced/absent from the Markdown. Consistent with Volume 59 policy, the numeral is preserved and the omitted Soviet apparatus is not imported.

The direct French pronoun mismatch in “the future appears to us like a luminous point before you” is preserved rather than silently harmonized; the editors’ Russian rendering separately smooths it to “the future appears bright ahead.”
The Russian code-switch Всегда собьюсь is rendered I always go astray and remains set off in both conceptual positions.
je n’ai pas dérangé mes finances ni arrangé is kept as not disordering the finances but not putting them in order either, preserving Tolstoy’s self-correction.
